GRADE SELECTION GUIDE
CHOOSING THE RIGHT BITUMEN GRADE BY APPLICATION

LAST REVIEWED SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 · PETROBIND EXPORT DESK

Bitumen is not one product — penetration grade, viscosity grade, polymer-modified, oxidized, and emulsion binders each suit a different application. Choosing the wrong family costs more than a bad price ever could, in rework or premature failure.

Request Bitumen Quote
View Bitumen Grades
ROAD AND PAVEMENT CONSTRUCTION

Penetration grades like 60/70 and 80/100, or viscosity grades VG 30/VG 40, are the standard choice for hot-mix asphalt, highways, airport runways, and urban roads. Harder grades (60/70, VG 40) suit hot climates and heavy traffic; softer grades (80/100) suit moderate climates and better low-temperature workability.

ROOFING, WATERPROOFING, AND COATINGS

Oxidized (blown) bitumen is preferred here for its higher softening point and stronger adhesion — used in roofing membranes, waterproofing systems, pipe coatings, mastics, sealants, and electrical insulation, where paving-grade bitumen would be too soft and temperature-sensitive.

MAINTENANCE AND COLD APPLICATION

Bitumen emulsion — a water-based dispersion, anionic or cationic — is used for tack coat, prime coat, surface dressing, slurry seal, and pothole patching where heating equipment isn't practical or a faster, safer, lower-temperature application is needed.

PMB (polymer-modified bitumen) for high-stress pavements needing extra elasticity and rutting resistance.

Oxidized bitumen for roofing, waterproofing, and industrial coatings.

Emulsion for tack coat, maintenance, and cold-mix applications.
